note.note:
Consult Summary:
- Telehealth consult for new-onset severe constant headache x 3 days with photophobia and visual phenomena in a woman on a combined oral contraceptive; clinician suspects possible migraine and arranged in-person neurological and fundoscopic exam, BP check, and trial of a stronger NSAID plus acetaminophen, with ER precautions if worsening.

History:
- Presenting complaint: “Blinding” headache for 3 days, constant, interfering with ability to work.
- Onset/duration/progression: Sudden onset upon awakening 3 days ago; continuous since; partially relieved by ibuprofen but never fully resolves.
- Location/character: Diffuse; worse over the right supraorbital area; described as severe and constant; brief stabbing pain with standing quickly; sensation “something moving” with abrupt head movement.
- Severity: Up to 8/10; decreases to ~5/10 with ibuprofen.
- Associated symptoms:
  - Photophobia (light sensitivity).
  - Visual phenomena described as “shooting lights”/weird vision.
  - Mild nausea; no vomiting.
  - No tingling, numbness, or weakness.
  - No change in smell or taste.
  - Sleep preserved; not waking from sleep; present on awakening.
  - Not clearly worse with cough/Valsalva; positional brief stabbing pain when standing quickly.
- Pertinent negatives:
  - No fever reported; temperature not checked.
  - No upper respiratory symptoms, sinus pain, sore throat, ear pain, cough, sputum.
  - No nosebleeds or hemoptysis.
  - No recent travel.
  - No unintentional weight change; reports low energy likely due to headache.
- Impact/function: Works from home; missed part/all of work over the last 3 days due to inability to focus.
- Prior headaches: Intermittent mild headaches previously; typically relieved by ibuprofen; no prior prolonged episodes or typical migraine features historically.
- Eye care: Recent optometry check reportedly unchanged.

Past Medical History:
- No chronic conditions reported.
- Remote history of unspecified pain in youth; resolved; no cause found.

Medications:
- Combined oral contraceptive pill (exact product not documented); started ~1 year ago; no side effects noted; no perceived change in headache frequency until current episode. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Ibuprofen as needed for headache (OTC). Dose/route/frequency not documented.
- Planned: “Stronger” NSAID similar to ibuprofen to be prescribed; instructed may take with acetaminophen concurrently. Specific medication/dose/route/frequency not documented.

Allergies:
- No known drug allergies.

Social History:
- Lives alone; works from home.
- Tobacco: Never smoker.
- Alcohol: Approximately 3 drinks once weekly (patient estimate; exact quantity/type not fully specified).
- No recreational drug use reported.
- No recent travel.

Family History:
- Mother with severe migraines (with vomiting). No other family history reported.

Physical Examination:
- None performed (teleconsult; in-person exam planned).
- Vitals: Not obtained.

Investigations:
- None conducted at this visit.
- Patient reports recent optometry/vision check without change.

Assessment & Plan:
- Issue 1: New severe continuous headache with photophobia and visual phenomena (3 days), right supraorbital predominance; mild nausea; no focal deficits.
  - Assessment: Clinician impression is possible migraine-type headache; features also consistent with migraine with visual symptoms. Secondary causes cannot be excluded without examination.
  - Plan:
    - Arrange in-person visit for complete neurological examination and fundoscopic evaluation.
    - Check blood pressure at visit.
    - Start prescribed stronger NSAID (specific agent not documented); take with food. May take acetaminophen concurrently. Dose/route/frequency not documented.
    - Safety net: If headache becomes unbearable, worsens, or changes character before the appointment, go to the Emergency Department (A&E) and/or call clinic for advice.
    - If symptoms fully resolve before scheduled exam, appointment may be canceled per clinician.
- Issue 2: Combined oral contraceptive use in context of possible migraine with visual symptoms.
  - Assessment: On combined OCP for ~1 year; if migraines with flashing lights/visual aura are confirmed, current pill may be inappropriate.
  - Plan:
    - Review BP and overall suitability of combined OCP at in-person visit.
    - If migraine with aura is confirmed, discuss switching contraception per clinician.
    - Continue current OCP for now per clinician guidance.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
- Migraine with aura (possible status migrainosus) – Likelihood: High.
  - Reasoning: Severe headache with photophobia and positive visual phenomena; right supraorbital emphasis; mild nausea; family history; persistent over several days with partial NSAID response.
- Cerebral venous sinus thrombosis (CVST) – Likelihood: Moderate.
  - Reasoning: New persistent severe headache in a woman on an estrogen-containing OCP; visual symptoms and some positional elements; absence of neurologic deficits lowers but does not eliminate risk.
- Tension-type headache – Likelihood: Low–Moderate.
  - Reasoning: Constant diffuse pain could fit; severity and migrainous features (photophobia, visual phenomena, nausea) argue against pure tension-type.

Quality checks:
- Missing expected elements: Vitals (including temperature, BP); full neurological exam; fundoscopic findings; medication names/doses/routes/frequencies for new prescription; pregnancy status; detailed headache red flag screen (e.g., neck stiffness, thunderclap timing, exertional/cough triggers); comprehensive past medical and surgical history; detailed alcohol quantity/type.
- Conflicts between transcript and DDx: None noted.
- Transcript quality: Some audio gaps/inaudible sections; OCP brand not captured; otherwise adequate for key history.
